advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the availability test expect True only when the libc is glibc (e.g. platform.libc_ver()[0] == 'glibc'), not whenever sys.platform starts with 'linux'
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:69: `"""Return glibc's ``malloc_trim``, or ``None`` where the C library lacks it (macOS, musl)."""`
advisory.finding: test_release_freed_heap_reports_availability expects release_freed_heap() to be True on every Linux, but the code says musl libc has no malloc_trim and returns False there. On a musl-based (e.g. Alpine) Linux runner the test fails even though the code is working as designed.
scenarios: CI or a dev container on an Alpine/musl Python image: sys.platform is 'linux' but _malloc_trim() returns None, so the assertion fails
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `import platform; expected = platform.libc_ver()[0] == "glibc"` and `assert release_freed_heap() is expected`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip the RSS test unless the libc is glibc and the build is not free-threaded (and/or turn the unmet precondition into pytest.skip)
evidence: tests/unit/test_mcp_idle_heap_release.py: `assert held["after_free"] - baseline > 128, (` / `"precondition: glibc should still hold the freed pages before the gauge goes idle; "`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:259: `leprous-uncivic-crab; free-threaded CPython exposes the gap)` — the project exercises free-threaded CPython, whose allocator is mimalloc, not glibc arenas
advisory.finding: The RSS test is gated only on sys.platform == linux, but its precondition (>128 MiB still resident after free) relies on CPython's raw allocator going through a glibc per-thread arena. On musl, on free-threaded CPython (which uses mimalloc and is called out in this module), or under different MALLOC_ARENA_MAX/tunables, the test fails with an AssertionError instead of being skipped.
scenarios: A free-threaded (3.13t) test run: freed string memory never sits in a glibc arena, so the >128 MiB precondition is not met and the test fails
A musl runner: malloc_trim is absent and the allocator behaves differently, so either assertion can fail
advisory.suggested_fix: Skip when `platform.libc_ver()[0] != "glibc"` or `sysconfig.get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED")`, and replace the precondition assert with `if ...: pytest.skip("allocator did not retain freed pages")`.

dropped.finding: The end-to-end RSS test measures `baseline` without trimming first, then hard-asserts that the worker grew RssAnon by more than 128 MiB. If an earlier test on the same xdist worker left freed pages in a thread arena, the new thread can reuse that arena. Its allocations then fill pages already counted in the baseline, the growth stays under 128 MiB, and the test fails based on test order rather than on the behaviour under test.
merged_from: The end-to-end RSS test is skipped only when the platform is not Linux. Its precondition and its final assertion both depend on glibc's malloc owning str allocations. On a free-threaded CPython build, objects come from mimalloc, which malloc_trim does not manage, and CI runs a free-threaded 3.14t sweep on Linux. The skip guard does not cover that environment, so the test fails there for reasons unrelated to the change.

The new fallback path, where libc has no malloc_trim and `_malloc_trim()` returns None so release_freed_heap() returns False and the gauge still settles to zero without raising, is never run by gating CI. The only test that reaches it is the platform-conditional availability test. Gating CI runs it only on Linux (the True path), because the macOS gating cell runs only the path-selected platform_compat subset and this file is not in it.
scenarios: A memory-heavy test that uses worker threads runs earlier on the same xdist worker, leaving a large freed arena. This test's thread reuses it, after_free - baseline is about 0, and the precondition assertion fails even though the trim works.
dropped.suggested_fix: Call `release_freed_heap()` right before `baseline = _rss_anon_mib()` so the baseline starts from a trimmed heap. Optionally, turn the precondition into `pytest.skip(...)` when the allocator did not keep the pages, so an environment difference shows up as a skip rather than a false failure.
